messages:
sara: :rotating_light: Pager triggered — eu-west-1 decode pool (eu-decode-03) flapping. Multiple CUDA exceptions and OOM traces, several streaming responses cut off mid-token.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-3456 created (severity: s2). Affected path: streaming/decode. Observed ~3.2% request drops in last 6m.
mike: acked. i'm oncall, joining. pulling live logs and metrics now.
alen: memory graphs show steady KV cache growth on long-lived streams; a subset of requests report max_tokens headers in the 10k-100k range — looks like runaway generation.
sara: sample GPU backtrace from eu-decode-03: ```cudaExceptionIllegalAddress at gpu_decode.cu:399\nGPU free: 180MB, required: 1.1GB``` — kernel failing when attempting large KV allocations.
mike: immediate mitigations we can do: 1) enforce max_tokens at router to trim incoming extremes, 2) fallback some workers to a smaller model variant. who can flip router flag?
tim: i can push the router flag now. executing: `POST /control/flags {"enforce_max_tokens":true, "max_tokens_default":2048}`
ops-bot: Flag update applied by tim. Enforcement active for eu-west-1 router set.
alen: after flag: routers are rejecting headers >2048 (400). rejections ~1.6% of incoming streaming traffic so far. memory pressure starting to ease on some nodes.
customer-success-bot: pinging @rachel — some customers already reported partial outputs. recommend a short CS blurb.
rachel: drafting update to impacted customers: "We're investigating intermittent decode failures in eu-west-1 affecting streaming outputs. We've applied temporary generation caps to protect stability; you may see truncated or rejected long-running streams. We're actively mitigating and will follow up with a timeline." sending now.
mike: next step — canary fallback to reduce memory usage: route a fraction of decode traffic to llama-4-small variant on suspect workers. rolling canary to 10%.
sara: canary patch: `PATCH /nodes/eu-decode-*/config {"fallback_variant":"llama4-small","accept_large_max_tokens":false}` — applied to 10% (eu-decode-03a,b).
alen: canary nodes show ~35% lower resident GPU memory and no OOMs during stress windows. promising.
mike: ramping to 50% but watching for regressions.
alen: also enabling idle-stream eviction to reclaim KV quickly: `evict_idle_streams(timeout=60s)`. early telemetry shows reclaimed several GBs across the pool.
tim: note — we did a soft reboot of two workers earlier which produced brief 502s; added to post-incident notes.
sara: adding heavy logging for any request that generates >50k tokens with trace ids for postmortem.
alen: root-cause hypothesis so far: legacy/third-party SDKs sending malformed or extreme max_tokens headers combined with lack of router-side caps allowed runaway generation. that plus GPU memory fragmentation and KV growth exposed a cudaIllegalAddress in the decode kernel.
mike: mitigations and follow-ups: 1) default router max_tokens (global), 2) predecode header validation (reject unrealistic values), 3) telemetry alert on per-request token growth, 4) kernel hardening for sparse KV growth, 5) SDK patch to sanitize token caps for clients.
sara: creating ticket INC-2026-3456-RT and assigning owners: sara -> 1 & 3, alen -> 4, rachel -> comms.
alen: i'll take kernel triage with research and schedule a memory-defrag experiment in staging.
rachel: CS update sent: affected orgs notified; drafted FAQ for customers about temporary caps and next steps.
mike: status update: region degraded but stabilizing. request drops down from ~3.2% -> 0.4% after router cap + canary rollout + eviction. OOMs no longer observed on canary nodes.
incident-bot: oncall rotation in ~22m. if OOMs reappear, escalate to eng-runtime. next automated update in 30m or on state change.
sara: thanks all. i'll compile a postmortem draft after kernel triage. please add any missing notes to the JIRA. :thumbsup:
